AAON_2017q3: AAON entered Q2 2017 with weak trailing earnings but a noticeably better order picture. Q1 sales had been roughly flat and net income down 11.5%, yet backlog rose to about $68.9 million and management said order intake strengthened late in the quarter. Q2 itself remained soft—revenue fell about 1% to $101.3 million and net income declined 6.3%—so the +4.32% two-day move cannot be explained by the headline quarter alone. The most plausible interpretation is that investors looked through the weak recognized results toward the earlier recovery in orders/backlog, while the modest sales decline suggested the business was not entering a severe demand contraction. Contemporary indexed coverage is thin for this 2017 observation, so the causal ranking is explicitly inferential rather than presented as confirmed fact.
AAON_2018q4: AAON entered Q3 2018 with record demand but poor earnings conversion. Q2 sales had risen 8.2% and backlog jumped 87.5% to $156.6 million, while net income fell 15.2%, making manufacturing productivity, raw-material costs and pricing the main investor concerns. Q3 then missed consensus—EPS was $0.27 versus $0.30 and revenue also fell short—yet management said the problem was operational: new manufacturing technology, labor availability and low productivity among recent hires. Importantly, record backlog remained intact, slower hiring was already improving throughput, warranty costs were easing, and prior price increases were expected to support future margins. The +12.30% two-day move therefore looks less like a reaction to the headline quarter and more like a re-rating of the probability that AAON could convert strong demand into better margins in 2019.
AAON_2019q2: AAON entered Q1 2019 after a difficult margin year but with a well-established recovery thesis. Record 2018 sales and backlog contrasted with labor problems, raw-material inflation and production inefficiencies; management argued that prior price increases and better training/productivity would improve 2019 margins. The stock had already rallied strongly—Zacks noted roughly 42% YTD appreciation versus about 17% for the S&P 500—so expectations were elevated. Q1 was mixed against consensus: adjusted EPS of $0.21 missed $0.24, but revenue beat and grew 15% year over year. More importantly, net income rose sharply, backlog reached $166 million, and management explicitly credited pricing, productivity and higher volume for improving gross margins. The +2.98% two-day move is therefore best understood as confirmation of the margin-recovery/backlog thesis, tempered by the fact that adjusted EPS still missed consensus.
AAON_2019q4: AAON entered Q3 2019 with strong backlog but a known manufacturing-capacity problem. Q2 had missed consensus, and management said sheet-metal equipment downtime was limiting output even as backlog stayed high; eight new Salvagnini systems and a $28 million Longview expansion were intended to solve the constraint. Q3 showed only limited progress: sales rose just 0.5% and net income fell 1.8%, with management again identifying sheet-metal production as the bottleneck. New machines had started coming online in mid-September and maintenance capacity was improving, so the problem still looked operational rather than demand-driven. The -1.76% two-day move is therefore most plausibly tied to slower-than-hoped conversion of backlog into sales and earnings, with new capacity and long-term investment preventing a more severe negative reaction.
AAON_2020q1: AAON's February 2020 report was the clearest test yet of whether its 2019 capacity investments had solved the sheet-metal bottleneck. Q4 answered positively: sales rose 9.1% to $122.6 million, net income increased 33.2% to $17.3 million, and management cited new fabrication equipment, better workforce utilization, prior price increases and lower warranty costs. That directly addressed the operational issue that had held back Q2 and Q3. The +8.44% two-day return is particularly notable because the S&P 500 was simultaneously collapsing into a coronavirus-driven correction. The most probable driver was therefore confirmation of a real margin/throughput inflection, followed by operating leverage from pricing and efficiency, with high backlog and continued investment supporting the forward view.
AAON_2020q2: AAON entered Q1 2020 with improving factory execution but a completely new external risk from COVID-19. Before earnings, the company demonstrated operational resilience by running around the clock to supply customized HVAC units for a temporary New York hospital, while also managing an operations-leadership transition. Q1 then delivered 20.8% revenue growth and a 149.5% increase in net income. Management credited added manufacturing capacity, shorter lead times, near-100% on-time delivery and better fixed-cost absorption, while saying the business had experienced minimal pandemic disruption to that point. The most probable driver of the +1.06% two-day move was the extraordinary earnings leverage, followed by evidence of COVID resilience and reassurance that lower backlog partly reflected faster shipments rather than solely weaker demand.
AAON_2021q4: AAON entered Q3 2021 with very strong demand but growing inflation and supply-chain pressure. Q2 had produced record sales, rapidly rising backlog and very strong bookings, while management warned that labor and raw-material costs were hurting profitability. Q3 generated $138.6 million of revenue and $0.29 EPS, but SEC-hosted company figures showed gross profit down and gross margin falling to 26.0% from 30.3%. At the same time, backlog remained at a record level. The +1.02% two-day move therefore looks like a mixed verdict: investors retained confidence in demand and future backlog conversion, but did not receive the margin normalization they were waiting for. Strong prior stock performance—AP noted roughly 11% YTD and 24% over twelve months—also raised the bar for a larger positive surprise.
AAON_2022q3: AAON entered Q2 2022 with investors already frustrated that strong demand was not translating into sufficient profit. Inflation, supply-chain disruption and older low-priced backlog had compressed margins, while the stock had weakened alongside both company-specific earnings disappointment and a difficult broad market. Q2 repeated that split: revenue rose 45.1% to $208.8 million and beat consensus, but EPS of $0.30 missed the $0.41 estimate. BasX and legacy volume were strong, and backlog reached a record $464 million, up 235.9% year over year. Management also said the backlog's margin profile was improving as newer price increases entered orders. The -2.40% two-day move is therefore best explained first by the EPS/margin miss, second by the delay before pricing fully offsets inflation, and third by record backlog/BasX demand limiting concern about the long-run growth story.
AAON_2023q1: AAON entered Q4 2022 with a much better setup than it had six months earlier: pricing and production efficiency were beginning to catch up with inflation, and the key question was whether record backlog could convert into both volume and margin growth. The stock was up only about 2.8% over the prior three months, leaving room for a surprise. Q4 delivered one: EPS of $0.71 beat $0.56 consensus and revenue of $254.6 million beat roughly $240.3 million expected. Sales rose 86.8%, with large contributions from organic volume, pricing and BasX, while gross margin reached 30.8% as supply-chain and productivity conditions improved. Backlog still ended at a record $548 million. The +11.53% two-day move is therefore most plausibly driven by a decisive profitability inflection, successful backlog conversion into record production, and continued forward visibility from an order book that remained extremely strong.
AAON_2024q1: AAON entered Q4 2023 after a year of unusually strong execution, so the market's hurdle was high. The company had already moved from a margin-recovery story to one centered on sustaining exceptional productivity, margins and backlog growth despite tougher comparisons. Q4 beat consensus—EPS was $0.56 versus $0.53 and revenue was $306.6 million versus roughly $294.4 million—while gross margin remained excellent at 36.4% and backlog improved. Yet management also acknowledged softer nonresidential construction and tougher 2024 comparisons, and MarketBeat showed the shares down in extended trading. The -2.48% two-day move is therefore best interpreted as an expectations/growth-rate reset: the quarter was objectively strong, but investors were already pricing very high execution and focused more on the possibility of slower 2024 growth than on the modest earnings beat.
AAON_2024q4: AAON entered Q3 2024 with extremely strong momentum. Q2 had beaten revenue and EPS expectations by wide margins, the stock rose immediately after the release, and the company had largely resolved first-quarter production issues. The most important event before Q3 was the October 25 announcement of roughly $174.5 million in liquid-cooling orders from a data-center customer, which substantially strengthened the BASX growth narrative. By November 7, Investing.com put the stock up about 37.4% over three months. Q3 then delivered another beat—$327.25 million revenue versus $315.8 million consensus and $0.63 EPS versus $0.57—while BasX sales grew strongly. Gross margin did decline to 34.9% from 37.2%, creating a real offset. The +13.76% two-day move is therefore most plausibly explained by validation of the data-center/BASX growth thesis plus another clean earnings beat, with margin compression viewed as a secondary and likely temporary concern.
